knowledge:
- key_parameters: no.peaks=The number of peaks of interest detected in the mass spectrometry experiment ;; no.replicates=The intended number of technical replicates per biological sample (typically 2) ;; threshold=The correlation threshold (e.g., 0.80) used to filter out samples with inconsistent replicate peak information ;; intraclasscorr=The intraclass correlation between technical replicates (e.g., 0.60), representing the proportion of total variance due to biological variation ;; signifcut=The significance level cut-off (typically 0.05) used to control the false positive rate ;; Z=The heterogeneity correction factor representing sample imbalance and confounding effects (Z = 2 indicates a perfectly balanced study; Z > 2 indicates imbalance)
- alternatives: PROcess=Bioconductor package for pre-processing raw SELDI mass spectra, which can be used before clippda ;; caMassClass=Bioconductor package for pre-processing and classification of SELDI datasets ;; limma=The dupcor function in limma is used internally for handling duplicate correlations, but clippda provides specialized wrappers for sample size calculations ;; Cairns et al. (2009) method=An alternative sample size calculation that ignores confounder information, which may underestimate the required sample size
- when_to_use: Use this package when planning a clinical proteomic profiling study (SELDI or MALDI) to calculate the required biological sample size to achieve adequate statistical power, or when pre-processing and formatting mass spectrometry datasets with technical replicates to resolve mislabelling and filter out inconsistent replicates.
- pitfalls: Mislabelling of samples leading to incorrect numbers of replicates (some with none, some with more than two) which must be pre-processed ;; Ignoring confounding factors and sample imbalances at the design stage, which leads to underestimating the required sample size ;; Directly transferring sample size parameters from microarray studies to proteomics, which is inappropriate because proteomics studies typically have far fewer peaks (45-150) than microarrays have genes (thousands) ;; High biological variance inflating the required sample size, which must be carefully controlled

workflows.name: clinical_proteomics_sample_size_planning
workflows.intent: Pre-process raw mass spectrometry peak data with technical replicates, format it with phenotypic covariates into an S4 object, and calculate the required sample size for a clinical proteomic study.
input: raw_mass_spec_peaks.csv (Dataframe of raw peak intensities with columns SampleTag, CancerType, Spectrum, Peak, Intensity, Substance.Mass)
phenotypic_data.csv (Dataframe of sample phenotypic information with columns SampleTag, tumor, sex)
workflows.stages: 1. Check the number of replicates per sample using checkNo.replicates ;; 2. Pre-process repeated peak data using preProcRepeatedPeakData to resolve mislabelling and select the most similar replicates ;; 3. Filter out samples with low replicate correlation using spectrumFilter ;; 4. Format the data into a clustered structure using sampleClusteredData ;; 5. Combine expression and phenotypic data into an aclinicalProteomicsData S4 object ;; 6. Extract expression and phenotypic data using proteomicsExprsData and proteomicspData ;; 7. Estimate biological and technical parameters using sampleSizeParameters ;; 8. Calculate the heterogeneity correction factor Z using fisherInformation ;; 9. Compute the required sample sizes using sampleSize ;; 10. Visualize sample size requirements using sampleSizeContourPlots and sampleSize3DscatterPlots
workflows.code:
data(liverRawData)
data(liver_pheno)
no.peaks <- 53
no.replicates <- 2
checkNo.replicates(liverRawData,no.peaks,no.replicates) 
threshold <- 0.80 
Data <- preProcRepeatedPeakData(liverRawData, no.peaks, no.replicates, threshold)
TAGS <- spectrumFilter(Data,threshold,no.peaks)$SampleTag
NewRawData2 <- Data[Data$SampleTag %in% TAGS,]
JUNK_DATA <- sampleClusteredData(NewRawData2,no.peaks)
OBJECT=new("aclinicalProteomicsData")
OBJECT@rawSELDIdata=as.matrix(NewRawData2)
OBJECT@covariates=c("tumor" ,    "sex")
OBJECT@phenotypicData=as.matrix(liver_pheno)
OBJECT@variableClass=c('numeric','factor','factor')
OBJECT@no.peaks=no.peaks
OBJECT
head(proteomicsExprsData(OBJECT))
head(proteomicspData(OBJECT))
intraclasscorr  <-  0.60 
signifcut <- 0.05  
Data=OBJECT
sampleSizeParameters(Data, intraclasscorr, signifcut)
Z <- as.vector(fisherInformation(Data)[2,2])/2
Z 
sampleSize(Data, intraclasscorr, signifcut)
